The mechanical gate and the four questions passed; the review raised five false-positive/accuracy findings against the skill's own 'no false positives' bar, and all five were fixed before this entry.

Five no-FP tests added.

findings.finding: HEADLINE fired on git 'cherry-pick' vocabulary and 'most favorable way' with no escape hatch.
findings.resolution: fixed: scoped HEADLINE_CHERRY to the reporting sense (headlined/cherry-picked the favorable result/cut/metric); git cherry-pick and 'most favorable way' now pass. No-FP test added.

findings.finding: the comparison pattern 'is more \w+ than' over-matched ordinary comparatives ('more work/common than'), and ADR-0093 described the trigger as tighter than the code.
findings.resolution: fixed: replaced the wildcard with a curated adjective set (more reliable/secure/robust/...); corrected the ADR Consequences line to match. No-FP test added.

findings.finding: the observed/inferred tally was document-global, so unrelated counts could bind to an unrelated 'done' claim.
findings.resolution: fixed: the tally is now local to the done claim's line + adjacent evidence row, and only applies in an evidence/records context. No-FP test added.

findings.finding: the 'now <state>' trigger flagged ordinary English ('now reported to the vendor', 'now inferred from the header'), with no state able to clear it.
findings.resolution: fixed: DOWNGRADE_CLAIM now requires an explicit downgrade verb (downgrad*/lowered/dropped/moved to <state>); the bare 'now <state>' trigger was dropped. No-FP test added.

findings.finding: OWNS_CLAIM flagged ordinary domain facts ('the user owns their data', 'the team is responsible for triage'); by-design but noisy, and inconsistent with the VERIFY domain-exemption precedent.
findings.resolution: fixed: OWNS_CLAIM scoped to a code-ownership context (a code noun, or an 'assume'); domain facts now pass while a code-ownership assumption without an owner record/state is still flagged. No-FP test added.
